correctness.rationale: Every edge without C–R type is a positive-potential matching or mismatch indicator with exact unilateral utility increments; integer boundedness excludes all strict-improvement cycles. On a C–R edge, use two actions unoccupied by stubborn vertices and hold all other flexible agents at a third action. Four alternating endpoint changes each improve utility by exactly one without touching any other match/mismatch; so a directed cycle exists for every cross-type edge. The three-vertex equilibrium and binary path transition graph are enumerated analytically. The independent-definition finite checker reproduces 6600 cases and 203904 potential identities but the proof does not infer infinity from tests.

value.rationale: FIP is a natural global convergence certificate for decentralized network games, strictly stronger than existence of pure Nash equilibrium. The equivalence classifies every finite graph without connectedness/degree restrictions under a natural common multi-action and pinned-color regime; the two-unused-actions hypothesis has a direct mechanism, and the minimal three-node equilibrium/cycle coexistence distinguishes static solvability from process convergence. The sharp binary-path contrast demonstrates the assumption is not decorative.
